issues.problem: The revised requirement still contradicts itself on eligible group heads: it says the recipient user role is `head`, then immediately says `ReportingGroup.head` may be `head` or `admin`. The schema explicitly allows `headUserId` to reference a user with role `head` or `admin` (`prisma/schema.prisma:60`), and tasks/design also say `head`/`admin`. An implementer could literalize the SHALL text as `role = head`, pass the listed scenarios, and silently drop escalations for admin-led groups.
issues.fix: Make the normative requirement unambiguous: eligible heads are active users whose role is either `head` or `admin`, and add a test/task scenario for an admin-headed reporting group receiving the escalation digest.

issues.problem: The proposal promises a per-IP vitals limiter, but the current rate-limit factory keys from req.ip while the repo has a separate active change documenting that Express trust proxy is not set, so production req.ip collapses to the Caddy container. Evidence: harden-web-vitals-endpoint proposal lines 25-28 and design lines 99-104 promise a per-IP/minute limiter; apps/api/src/infrastructure/throttler/rate-limit.middleware.ts lines 40-42 keys from req.ip; openspec/changes/set-express-trust-proxy/design.md lines 3-17 documents that req.ip is currently the Caddy container without trust proxy. Implementing this as written can turn web-vitals ingestion into a global shared bucket and does not satisfy the stated per-client abuse boundary.
issues.fix: Add an explicit dependency/order on set-express-trust-proxy or change this proposal/spec/tasks to describe and test the real global-bucket stopgap until trust proxy is enabled; include a verification task that req.ip resolves to the client before claiming per-IP vitals throttling.

That contradiction can let an implementer skip required scrape-path work while still claiming the non-goal.

issues.problem: The cross-change dependency on enforce-smtp-config is still under-specified in a way that can produce an unresolvable Nest dependency. enforce-smtp-config allows ENV_CONFIG to live only in app.module.ts providers; AppModule imports HealthModule, but HealthModule's controller cannot inject a provider declared only in the importing AppModule. This change then says to reuse the existing token and not declare it twice, so if SMTP lands first using the app.module option, HealthController cannot resolve ENV_CONFIG.
issues.fix: Make the shared outcome mandatory: define ENV_CONFIG in a dedicated exported config module (or equivalent shared module), import it into both AppModule/EmailService's module scope and HealthModule, and update both changes' tasks/design to forbid the app.module-only provider option.

issues.problem: The navigation scenario only protects the queued drain from writing section-A content to section B, but the hook is reused across report/period navigation (`lead-form.tsx:718`) and has one global `lastSavedRef` (`use-lead-form-autosave.ts:80`). A section-A in-flight save that resolves after section B loads will still run `onSuccess` and overwrite the current baseline with `inFlightRef.current` (`use-lead-form-autosave.ts:103-106`) after `initialSavedKey` was primed from the newly loaded section (`lead-form.tsx:710-715`), making section B look dirty and scheduling a spurious save even when the user made no B edit.
issues.fix: Add a requirement/scenario/test for old-section in-flight completion after navigation, and capture/compare the in-flight section id before updating the current `lastSavedRef` baseline.

issues.problem: The archive pagination spec is internally inconsistent after moving pagination into the repository: it requires the DB query to read at most `limit` rows, but also requires `nextCursor` to be the last row only when more rows remain. Current code can know that because the service fetches and sorts the full archive before slicing; a repository query capped at exactly `limit` rows cannot know whether another row exists without an extra row/probe/count.
issues.fix: Specify the concrete DB-pagination contract: either fetch `limit + 1` rows and return only `limit` items, or perform an explicit existence probe/count; update the scenario wording and tasks/tests so `nextCursor` semantics are implementable without reintroducing full-archive reads.
